city.Somalia.description: This country curves around the Horn of Africa, the continent's easternmost tip, with a long coastline on the Indian Ocean. Its people are famous for camels, spoken poetry, and ancient trading ports.
city.Somalia.landmark: caravan of camels crossing golden dunes toward the turquoise Indian Ocean coast
city.Somalia.greeting: In Somali, hello is “Iska waran” (IS-ka wah-RAN).
city.Somalia.flag: plain sky-blue with a single white five-pointed star

city.South Sudan.description: South Sudan is the world's youngest country, born in 2011. This green land in the heart of Africa is known for the vast Sudd wetlands along the White Nile, huge herds of long-horned cattle, and one of the planet's greatest antelope migrations.
city.South Sudan.landmark: herders with long-horned cattle among the reeds of the vast Sudd wetland at dawn
city.South Sudan.greeting: English is official here, but you'll also hear “Salaam” (sah-LAAM) in Juba Arabic.
city.South Sudan.flag: black, red, and green bands with a gold star in a blue triangle
city.South Sudan.clue.0: circled the world's newest country on a map, deep in the heart of Africa
city.South Sudan.clue.1: kept talking about a giant swamp where the White Nile spreads into endless green reeds
city.South Sudan.clue.2: asked the bank for a bundle of South Sudanese pounds before setting off
city.Sudan.description: Sudan is a big desert country in northeast Africa, where the Blue Nile and White Nile join together at its capital, Khartoum. It is famous for having even more ancient pyramids than Egypt, built long ago by Nubian kings.
city.Sudan.flag: red, white, and black stripes with a green triangle at the pole
city.Sudan.clue.0: couldn't wait to see hundreds of steep, narrow pyramids rising from the sand
city.Sudan.clue.1: kept talking about a city where the Blue Nile and White Nile flow together
city.Tanzania.description: Tanzania is an East African country home to Mount Kilimanjaro, the continent's highest peak, and the Serengeti plains, where millions of wildebeest migrate each year. Off its coast lie the spice islands of Zanzibar, once a hub of Swahili trade.
city.Tanzania.flag: pinned on a flag badge: green and blue halves split by a black stripe edged in gold
city.Tanzania.clue.0: dreamed of climbing Africa's tallest mountain, capped with snow near the equator
city.Tanzania.clue.1: wanted to watch millions of wildebeest and zebra thunder across the grasslands
city.Tanzania.clue.2: studied a guidebook page picturing Tanzanian shilling notes
city.Togo.description: Togo is a narrow, ribbon-shaped country in West Africa, stretching from beaches on the Gulf of Guinea up to savanna hills. It is known for the mud tower-houses of Koutammakou and the busy Vodun markets of its seaside capital, Lome.
